diagnoses.summary: PCA shows a large coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, with the strongest contributor coming from CSTR temperature. Rule-based hypothesis points to a distillate pump trip as the primary cause, supported by the active DISTILLATE train fault and P202_TRIP alarm.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset dominated by CSTR temperature rise with accompanying pressure rise and alarms on reactor pressure; strong indication of a heater fault causing excessive heat input, with secondary contribution from pressure control/PCV issues.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations and a saturated temperature controller. The leading evidence points to an actuator fault in the CSTR heater causing an overtemperature condition, with possible accompanying sensor/controller anomalies.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The dominant contributor is the CSTR temperature measurement/control path, with the R_TIC loop saturated while the reactor temperature is rising and alarms for high temperature are active. The most likely cause is a stuck high heater (reactor heater) driving the temperature up, while the temperature controller cannot correct due to actuator saturation.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and a strong temperature excursion in the CSTR, with the R_TIC loop saturated but its PV still high. The fixed-rule and evidence point toward an actuator fault in the CSTR heater driving an overheating condition, with secondary impact from catalyst activity issues and a stuck/in-range limit in the temperature controller. One or more faults may be active.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset driven mainly by the CSTR temperature control loop (R_TIC) with loop saturation and a latched high-high SIF. The most consistent fault from the catalogue is an actuator issue at the CSTR heater causing an abnormal temperature/pressure response.

A coherent plant upset with large T2 and SPE, dominated by CSTR pressure signal (and related reactor measurements). The most consistent fault is an actuator issue at the H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve), likely capacity degradation causing mismatch between PCV command and actual opening, potentially with stuck-closed behavior contributing to abnormal pressure/temperature trends.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure/PCV behavior with large T2 and very large SPE, pointing to an H2 PCV related fault (capacity degradation or stuck). Upstream indicators (pressure) dominate the SPE, and several rule-based hypotheses center on the H2 PCV. Additional component-level faults (sensor bias) could be contributing but are secondary.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. Top contributions point to reactor temperature and pressure dynamics; several fault hypotheses from the catalogue could explain the observed pattern, with heater-related and catalyst/activity issues being most plausible.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with a strong contribution from the reactor temperature measurement and a very large SPE driven by op.R_TIC. The most plausible issue is a sensor fault on the R_TIC transmitter, with secondary possibilities of heater/reaction-rate related faults affecting the CSTR.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations. The strongest signals point to a sensor fault driving spurious correlation changes, with a possible actuator/safety fault contributing to the temperature/ heater behavior.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with strong contribution from CSTR temperature and TIC; likely a heater actuator fault causing elevated reactor temperature and correlated sensor/controller responses.

PCA flag indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor temperature rise driven by actuator/sensor faults around the CSTR. The strongest rule-based hints point to a stuck high CSTR heater, with possible contributing sensor bias and catalyst activity effects.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. Most consistent with an actuator fault in the reactor heater or a heater-related control/mismatch, supported by the rule evidence pointing to heater-related anomalies and a strong indication of a heater command–actual mismatch.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong temperature rise driver and correlated pressure effects, pointing to a reactor energy/chemistry upset. Rule-based hints favor a reactor heater anomaly (stuck/high) as the leading cause, with possible catalyst activity degradation contributing. H2 PCV issues are less supported by the evidence but remain as lower-probability alternatives.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with strong temperature controller involvement and actuator-level mismatch hints. Most likely a faulty CSTR heater actuator causing an anomalous heater output, leading to the observed temperature and pressure trajectory.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong contribution from CSTR temperature and reactor control actions. Likely a process degradation in catalyst activity driving acetone production issues, with possible heater-related mismatch contributing to temperature excursion.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong temperature rise in the CSTR and rising reactor pressure, best explained by a CSTR heater anomaly leading to elevated reactor temperature, with supporting signs of degraded catalytic activity. PCV related faults are possible but less likely as primary cause.
High-dimensional process upset with large, coherent movement; most likely a reactor heater issue propagating through temperature, with catalyst activity impact also plausible.

PCA flags a strong, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations. Top contributors point to a temperature rise in the CSTR and actuator/controller interactions near the CSTR outlet. Rule-based hints favor a heater fault or catalyst activity loss, with heater fault being most likely given the prominent temperature deviation and heater-related control signals.
PCA abnormality with high T² and high SPE indicates a coherent upset likely due to an actuator-driven heater issue causing elevated reactor temperature and related process shifts.

A large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by reactor temperature anomaly and reactor pressure contributions, best explained by an actuator fault affecting the CSTR heater. Two additional plausible faults are catalyst activity loss and H2 PCV issues, but the strongest signal points to reactor heater actuator fault.
Abnormal operation with large, coherent elevation in reactor temperature driving a high overall process shift; heater actuator fault is most likely, with secondary sensor/process issues possible.
